findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

A knife on the magnetic strip is observed to be soiled on both sides of the blade. It is believed that the blade was not completely cleaned prior to storage. The PIC was shown and moved the knife to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

The faucet to the right of the dish machine appears to have a persistent leak at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all plumbing is maintained in good repair at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The wall siding to the right of a shelf behind the register is observed pulling away from the wall and allowing for crumb accumulation. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and reseal the siding prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Several locations throughout the facility are in need of minor repairs. Locations include: 1) the end of the bar on the salad prep cooler has a ball of tape being used as a safety measure; 2) the wall siding to the right of the front prep cooler is pulling away and exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable; 3) multiple small holes are observed in the wall above the mop sink; 4) several small holes on the side of the walk in cooler; 5) the paint on the wall next to the CFPM certificates is observed with a pair of bald spots where a rough surface is exposed. These locations were discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces around food and moisture are maintained in a smooth and easily cleanable state at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple items throughout the kitchen and prep areas do not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to storage. These items were shown to the PIC and moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct. Ensure that all dishes and utensils are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

1) Multiple tray lids are stored on a shelf soiled with old oil. Multiple loads are stored in a container with crumbs/dust in the bottom. Both items were shown to the PIC and they were moved to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they remain free of potential contamination prior to use.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

Multiple bowls to the right of the slicing station are observed with food splash on them. It is assumed that tomatoes being sliced on the table next to them are spraying onto them. The PIC was consulted and the bowls moved to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that cleaned/sanitized food contact items are protected from contamination until use. A shield of some kind was discussed as well as moving the bowls to another location.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The metal along the right side of the mop sink appears to have come loose from the sink, exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was consulted and instructed to re-seal it prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

A pair of tongs are observed stored with the handles in contact with meatballs in a reach in cooler. Employees are observed to wash hands but not use gloves when preparing foods out of this cooler. Ensure that utensils are stored with the hand contact sections out of contact with the foods between uses. The tongs were moved during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

Multiple locations in the facility need to be resealed to make them smooth and easily cleanable: 1) The wall/sink junction to the right of the pot sink; 2) the table/wall junction to the left of the woks; 3) two holes in the wall above the rear handwashing sink; 4) the wall behind the utensil storage to the right of the hand sink. Reseal all locations prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

A food employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet prior to getting a paper towel. Education conducted. Ensure that a clean barrier is used to turn off the faucet to prevent recontaminating the freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Paper towels are missing for the hand sink in the front bathroom. Paper towels were replaced during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

The walk in cooler appears to be malfunctioning. PIC was already aware and the maintenance company (Eichenauer Services) was on site during this inspection attempting repairs. All foods tested were showing internal temperatures between 53-55F. TCS foods were discarded during this inspection. Multiple items were observed to still be frozen in the freezer. These items were moved into other coolers until the walk in could be repaired.  Repairs could not be completed prior to inspector leaving, therefor a follow up is being awarded. Normal follow up time would land on Saturday. Due to this the follow up will be conducted on Monday unless verification can be received prior to the weekend that repairs have been completed.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

The single service utensils in the service area are stored in containers with dust/ food debris in the bottoms. Single service is not pre-wrapped in these containers. Utensils were discarded and the containers cleaned during this inspection to correct the violation. PIC is instructed to ensure that these containers are maintained clean moving foreword.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

1) Multiple containers of pan inserts and lids are observed soiled with foods debris. PIC instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. 2) The single service utensils in the service area are stored in containers with dust/ food debris in the bottoms. Single service is not pre-wrapped in these containers. PIC is instructed to ensure that these containers are maintained clean moving foreword.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Facility does not currently have a method to verify that the surface of dishes reaches critical temperature (165F) in the dish machine. Inspector discussed with the PIC and stated that a method is required. Most common suggestions included maximum registering thermometers and temperature based test strips. A small amount of test strips were acquired during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that some form of verification is maintained moving foreword.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Only one of the three current CFPMs at the facility has an allergen certification available. All CFPMs at the facility should maintain a current allergen awareness certification. ANSI accredited courses are available online. Ensure that certifications are acquired prior to the next routine inspection and maintained moving forward.

findings.citation_text: 2-301.12 (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Sauces in the cold well along the cookline observed out of temperature: fresca at 60F; rosa crema at 52F; and pesto cream at 54F (probed). Review of temp logs indicate that all sauces were 41F or below prior to opening at 11AM. PIC stated that the cooler sometimes struggles to hold temperature and that ice is often used to help the cooler (as was observed today). Upon realizing sauces were out of temperature, sauces were removed and more ice was added to the well. Prior to completion of inspection, sauces had cooled as follows: rosa crema at 46F; pesto cream at 38F; and lemon parm at 41F. Schedule maintenance/repair of cooler so that it holds foods at 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed the raw eggs in a carton being stored over RTE food. Ensure that raw foods are stored below RTE foods. Eggs moved during the inspection. 
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed an assortment of rags sitting on a cart in the rear of the facility that were damp and dirty. Ensure that if a rag is in use that it is stored in the sanitizer solution. If it is finished, then it should be placed in the dirty linen basket. Employee was made aware and rags were moved to dirty linen.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed mulitiple dirty bowls and dishes by the soup steam table. It appeared to be dried soup on them. Employee stated she would wash, rinse, and sanitize the dishes, then find a proper place to store them. Ensure that clean dishes are stored in a manner that prevents cross contamination. 
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the caulking at the two compartment sink in the rear of the facility to be beginning to become in disrepair. Ensure that the sink is maintained in good repair, as well as smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed two light fixtures in the back dry storage area that were missing. Manager states they have the light shields on order. Ensure that light shields are provided for every light in a food prep area. 
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed beef cooling in the walk in cooler which was reported to have been cooked approximately 20 minutes ago but the time that the cooling process began is not documented anywhere. Beef was 54F at this time. It was discussed that the time that the cooling process begins should be recorded to ensure potentially hazardous foods that are being cooled reach 70F within 2 hours and 41F or below within an additional 4 hours. 
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: CORRECTED> Observed boxes of single service lids and bowls stacked on the floor in the dry storage area to the left of the dish room. Boxes were stacked on top of milk crates during inspection to correct the violation.

It was discussed that sinks must drain quickly to avoid wastewater from splashing up and contaminating clean hands.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the sinks in the restrooms to be slow draining. Manager reported that a customer had left the water running in the men's restroom for some time prior to inspection. Maintain plumbing so sinks drain quickly in order to promote hand washing for the full 20 seconds and to avoid contaminated water from splashing on clean hands. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Two door standup cooler was 45F-56F. The external thermometer read at 37F-41F; air temp in the very top was 39F. Air temperature varied depending on the location: top half was 39F-45F & bottom half was 52F-56F. Noodles in the top half were 39F-41F.  Noodles in the bottom half were 55F. The noodles in the bottom of the cooler had just been pre-bowled (no violation cited for foods out of temp for that reason). All the noodle dishes in the bottom half of the cooler were moved to the walkin (holding below 41F) . The top half of the cooler was still ok to use at this time. The managers turned the thermostat down and will monitor the temperature. Any foods left over at the end of the night will be moved to the walkin cooler. Call for repairs if temperature in the bottom does not reach 41F/below.
